newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq gives U.N. draft of its food plan.
newsitem.headline: Iraq gives U.N. draft of its food plan.

text.p: Iraq has given the United Nations a preliminary draft of its food procurement and distribution plan to cover the next six months of oil exports, Iraq's U.N. coordinator said on Wednesday.
"We have received last night from the government of Iraq a preliminary draft of the (food) distribution plan," Staffan de Mistura told Reuters.
Iraq has held up partial exports pending the completion of its distribution plan. The U.N. Security Council renewed the limited sales deal on June 8.
"It is a good step in the right direction," de Mistura said, but added that Iraq's plan still needed to be worked on before submitting the draft to U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan for approval.
"Some important sectors are still missing, hence we will need more discussions prior to its submission to the U.N. secretary general," he said.

Iraq started limited exports in December last year and completed its $2 billion quota late in May. The U.N. has allowed partial sales in order that Iraq can satisfy the urgent needs of its people labouring under U.N. trade sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
